prompt: Which inequality is shown on the number line below? (An **open** circle means the value itself is **not** included.)

hint: Look at each end of the shaded part separately. Is the circle there filled in or left open?
explanation: The shading runs from $-1$ to $2$, so $x$ lies **between** those two numbers and the answer is one joined inequality.
The circle at $-1$ is filled, which means $-1$ itself is included, so that end uses $\le$: $-1 \le x$.
The circle at $2$ is open, which means $2$ itself is left out, so that end uses $<$: $x < 2$.
Putting both ends together gives $-1 \le x < 2$, which is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test values
steps: Try $x = -1$, which sits on the filled circle and so is included. Choices C and D say $-1 < x$, which rejects $-1$, so both are out.
Try $x = 2$, which sits on the open circle and so is left out. Choice C was already gone, and it would wrongly accept $2$.
Try $x = 5$, which is outside the shading. Choice A accepts it because $5 > 2$, so A is out as well.
Only $-1 \le x < 2$ accepts $-1$, rejects $2$ and rejects $5$, so the answer is choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compound-inequality shorthand
steps: A joined inequality such as $a \le x < b$ packs two facts into one line: $a \le x$ **and** $x < b$.
The left end of the shading is a filled circle at $-1$, so the left fact is $-1 \le x$.
The right end is an open circle at $2$, so the right fact is $x < 2$.
Writing both facts around one $x$ gives $-1 \le x < 2$, which is choice B.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: For a single endpoint: filled $= \le$ or $\ge$; open $= <$ or $>$. Now apply that rule to **both** ends of this segment.
Look at each end of the shaded part separately. Is the circle there filled in or left open?
The left circle at $-1$ is filled, so $-1$ is included. The right circle at $2$ is open, so $2$ is not. Pick the symbol that matches each end.
Filled at $-1$ and open at $2$ gives $-1 \le x < 2$, which is choice B.
